title: WPMS/1947/2022 of JASVEER SINGH Vs RAJENDRA KAUR

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No.1947 of 2022
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

Heard Mr. Pooran Singh Rawat,
Advocate for the petitioner.
Petitioner was tenant in respect of a
shop. The landlord, Sri Surendra Singh, filed
a suit for recovery of rent and ejectment of
petitioner from the said shop. The suit was
decreed. During pendency of the suit
Surendra Singh died and his legal
representatives were substituted. The
decree passed by trial Court was put to
execution.
Petitioner is aggrieved by an order
passed by Executing Court on 31.05.2022,
whereby he has been m ade liable to pay
` 77,664/ - towards use & occupation charges
in respect of shop in question.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
contends that as petitioner had vacated the
shop on 30.11.2019, therefore, he is not
liable to pay use & occupation charge for the
shop after 30.11.2019.
Learned Executing Court has considered
the report submitted by Court Am in, which

shows that vacant possession of the shop
was handed over to the Decree holder on
07.12.2021. Based on said report, petitioner
was m ade liable to pay use and occupation
charges upto 07.12.2021.
The report of the Court Amin is on
record, perusal whereof reveals that the
shop was lying vacant when it was opened
and its possession was handed over to the
landlord on 07.12.2021.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that since the shop was lying vacant
when Court Am in opened it, therefore,
petitioner cannot be m ade liable to charges
for its use and occupation.
Whether the shop was lying vacant or
petitioner's belonging were kept inside the
shop is not relevant. I f petitioner was
continuing to have physical possession of the
shop by putting his lock thereupon, then he
is liable to pay use & occupation charges.
The report of Court Amin reveals that
physical possession of the shop was handed
over to the landlord only on 07.12.2021,
therefore, learned Executing Court rightly
passed the order m aking petitioner liable to
pay use and occupation charges, upto
07.12.2021.

Thus, this Court does not find any
reason to interfere with the im pugned order.
Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is
dismissed.

( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
 22.08.2022
Arpan
